angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,837,344 km at 22.24 pc = 1.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 69701: distance 22.237 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.004), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 22.237 +/- 0.089 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 45.4014 +/- 0.2858 mas (same row, RUWE 3.74), 158.8 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 2.641 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 69701: radius 2.641 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 9.267 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.041) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 1,837,344 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 6201 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 69701: effective temperature 6201 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.025) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 69701: effective temperature 6201 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.025) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 683) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 3.67 from 2024A&A...683A.125P; the 34 published values span log g 2.926 to 4.2, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.3% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...683A.125P)
